messages:
alex: Heads-up — AcmeOps reporting a flood of 429s during their nightly fanout sync, all clustered at the top-of-minute. Looks like minute-window exhaustion around 02:00 UTC.

maya: Can you paste a sample request/response + headers so we can see the rate headers?

alex: Here’s the curl they sent: 
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"...","fanout":20}'
```
Response headers: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-minute: 1000/1000
x-rate-limit-second: 50/50
retry-after: 60
```

kevin: @alex can you pull gateway logs? That x-rate-limit-minute at 1000/1000 smells like they hit the token RPM/TPM. Common cause: client spawns many shards that all start at same second.

alex: Pasted filtered gateway logs for acct-acme: 
```
[02:00:00] request id=abc123 token=acct-acme path=/generate latency=120ms tokens=320
[02:00:00] request id=abc124 token=acct-acme path=/generate latency=130ms tokens=318
[02:00:00] request id=abc125 token=acct-acme path=/generate latency=115ms tokens=321
...
[02:00:00] throttle token=acct-acme window=minute limit=1000 used=1018
[02:00:05] throttle token=acct-acme window=minute limit=1000 used=1025
```

maya: That pattern confirms a fanout at the minute boundary. Immediate mitigations: ask customer to jitter start times across the minute, reduce parallelism, or use per-request batching so they can send N inputs in one request to reduce RPM.

sara_ops: I submitted a temporary minute-cap increase request for acct-acme to 5000 while they patch. Ticket INC-4872 created.

infra-bot: Alert: rate-limit-surge detected for token acct-acme — oncall notified.

kevin: For short-term guidance to the customer: implement client-side pacing snippet (spread 20 calls over 60s), honor Retry-After, and add exponential backoff with jitter so retries don't align. Long-term: recommend Dedicated capacity or a batch endpoint.

alex: I’ll reply to customer with a short snippet and sample jitter/backoff. Example Node pacing snippet I’ll include: 
```js
// spread 20 requests evenly over 60s
const total = 20;
for (let i=0;i<total;i++) {
  setTimeout(() => callApi(i), Math.floor((i/total) * 60000));
}
```

maya: Please also attach the exact per-minute counts (we need them for the postmortem and billing check).

alex: Added the per-minute counts to the support ticket and included a diagnostic gist.

sara_ops: Customer accepted temporary bump and will ship jitter in the next deploy — marking as in-progress :white_check_mark:.

kevin: Add to the internal playbook: "cron fanout anti-pattern" — include suggested client patterns (batching, jitter, token pacing) and a one-click sample to request a minute-cap bump.

alex: Will follow up once we have 24h stability confirmation. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
